content.value_statement: Schema.org research can be slow and inconsistent when extending a Logseq template graph. This skill compares official vocabulary with existing templates and recommends compatible classes, properties, types, and modules.
actual_capabilities: Researches public Schema.org class and property definitions.
Traces class inheritance, child classes, siblings, and inherited properties.
Maps Schema.org value types to Logseq property types.
Recommends single or multiple value cardinality for properties.
Compares vocabulary with existing Logseq template files.
Suggests modules, reusable properties, related classes, and implementation steps.
limitations: Requires network access to confirm the latest Schema.org definitions.
Recommendations depend on access to the target template files.
Cardinality choices may require project-specific judgment.
The included lookup scripts open documentation but do not parse it.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Template Class
use_cases.description: Research a Schema.org class before adding it, including hierarchy, properties, type mappings, module placement, and dependencies.

use_cases.title: Review Missing Properties
use_cases.description: Compare an existing class with official Schema.org properties and prioritize useful additions without duplicating inherited fields.

use_cases.title: Validate Data Modeling
use_cases.description: Check property ranges, Logseq types, cardinality, naming, and reuse before implementing a template change.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up a Class
prompt_templates.prompt: Research the Schema.org class [ClassName]. Give its definition, parent class, direct properties, and common use cases.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Property
prompt_templates.prompt: Research the Schema.org property [propertyName]. Recommend its Logseq type and cardinality, explain the mapping, and list relevant classes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare a Template Class
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [ClassName] in my Logseq template with Schema.org. Identify missing properties, inherited duplicates, reusable fields, and priority recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Integration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [ClassName] and the available template modules. Propose hierarchy placement, dependencies, property definitions, reuse opportunities, validation checks, and ordered implementation steps.

output_examples.input: Research the Recipe class before adding it to a Logseq template.
output: Recipe is a CreativeWork subtype for cooking instructions and related details.
Priority properties include recipeIngredient, recipeInstructions, cookTime, prepTime, and recipeYield.
Review NutritionInformation, HowToStep, and RestrictedDiet as related classes.

output_examples.input: Should birthDate use a date or text property?
output_examples.output: Use a Logseq date property with one value. Schema.org defines birthDate as Date, and a date field supports consistent entry and queries.

output_examples.input: What Person properties are missing from my template?
output_examples.output: The report compares current fields with Schema.org, groups missing properties by priority, and recommends types, cardinality, modules, and reuse.

best_practices: Provide the target class or property name and the relevant template files.
Confirm recommendations against the latest official Schema.org documentation.
Review inherited properties before creating new Logseq definitions.
anti_patterns: Do not add every available property without a concrete use case.
Do not duplicate inherited or shared properties in class-specific modules.
Do not treat suggested cardinality as mandatory when project requirements differ.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my Logseq template?
faq.answer: No. It researches vocabulary and provides recommendations unless you separately request implementation changes.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Current Schema.org verification requires network access. Local template comparison can proceed with available project files.

faq.question: Can it research both classes and properties?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers definitions, hierarchies, ranges, related vocabulary, Logseq type mappings, and cardinality.

faq.question: How does it choose a Logseq module?
faq.answer: It considers the class hierarchy, existing module patterns, related classes, and opportunities to reuse common properties.

faq.question: Can it detect duplicate properties?
faq.answer: Yes, when the target template files are available. It checks existing definitions and inherited properties before recommending additions.

faq.question: Are the included lookup scripts required?
faq.answer: No. They only open an official Schema.org page in the default browser for quick manual lookup.
